We have mass spec: m/z 276.066555... likely molecular ion [M+H]+? The formula we derived from isomers: C15H15O3S has exact mass? Let's calculate: C15=15*12=180, H15=15*1.007825=15.1174, O3=3*15.994915=47.9847, S=31.97207. Sum = 180+15.1174+47.9847+31.97207 = 275.07417. Add proton 1.007276 = 276.08145. Observed 276.0666, close. So formula C15H14O3S? That mass: C15=180, H14=14.10955, O3=47.9847, S=31.97207 = 274.0663, plus H+ = 275.0736. Not match. Observed 276.0666 suggests M+? maybe M+? If it's [M]+ (radical cation) mass 276.0666 corresponds to formula C15H14O3S? Let's compute exact monoisotopic mass of C15H14O3S: using atomic masses: C 12.0000, H 1.007825, O 15.994915, S 31.972071. So 15*12=180, 14*1.007825=14.10955, 3*15.994915=47.984745, S=31.972071. Sum = 273. (180+14.10955=194.10955; +47.984745=242.094295; +31.972071=274.066366). That's 274.0664. Not 276.0666. So maybe formula C15H16O3S? Add 2 H: 276.0820. That's close to observed 276.0666 (difference 0.0154). Could be C14H12O4S? Let's compute: C14=168, H12=12.0939, O4=63.97966, S=31.97207 total = 276.04563. Slightly low. Observed 276.0666. Could be C13H12O5S? 13*12=156, H12=12.0939, O5=79.974575, S=31.97207 total = 279. (156+12.0939=168.0939; +79.974575=248.068475; +31.97207=280.040545) too high.

Given mass spec peaks show isotopic pattern typical for sulfur (M+2 ~ 4% intensity). Observed intensities: M 100, M+1 16, M+2 33.6, M+3 5.27, etc. Sulfur gives M+2 about 4%? Actually 34S natural abundance 4.2% gives M+2 ~4% of M. Here M+2 intensity 33.6% which is high, maybe chlorine? Cl gives M+2 ~32% (35Cl 75%, 37Cl 25%). So pattern suggests presence of chlorine. But we have S? The isotopic pattern with M+2 ~33% suggests one chlorine atom. Also M+1 16% typical for C/H. So formula likely includes Cl. Let's compute formula with Cl: C15H15O3Cl? mass: C15 180, H15 15.1174, O3 47.9847, Cl 34.96885 (35Cl). Sum = 278.07095. That's higher than observed 276.0666. Maybe C14H13O3Cl? 14*12=168, H13=13.1017, O3=47.9847, Cl=34.9689 total = 263. (168+13.1017=181.1017; +47.9847=229.0864; +34.9689=264.0553). Not.

What about C13H11O3Cl2? Two Cl would give M+2 pattern ~64%? Not.

But observed M+2 intensity 33.6% suggests one Cl. So formula includes Cl. Let's compute exact mass for C14H12ClO2? 14*12=168, H12=12.0939, Cl=34.9689, O2=31.98983 total = 246. (168+12.0939=180.0939; +34.9689=215.0628; +31.9898=247.0526). Not.

Our mass 276.0666. Let's try C13H10ClO3? 13*12=156, H10=10.07825, Cl=34.9689, O3=47.9847 total = 249. (156+10.0783=166.0783; +34.9689=201.0472; +47.9847=249.0319). Not.

Maybe includes Br (79.9) gives M+2 ~100%? Not.

But pattern: M+2 33.6% suggests one Cl. So formula likely C15H14ClO2? Let's compute: C15 180, H14 14.10955, Cl 34.96885, O2 31.98983 total = 261. (180+14.10955=194.10955; +34.96885=229.0784; +31.98983=261.0682). Not.

We need 276.0666. Add maybe S also? Cl+S? Let's try C14H13ClO2S? C14 168, H13 13.1017, Cl 34.9689, O2 31.9898, S 31.9721 total = 279. (168+13.1017=181.1017; +34.9689=216.0706; +31.9898=248.0604; +31.9721=280.0325). Too high.

C13H11ClO3S? C13 156, H11 11.0861, Cl 34.9689, O3 47.9847, S 31.9721 total = 281. (156+11.0861=167.0861; +34.9689=202.055; +47.9847=250.0397; +31.9721=282.0118). Too high.

Maybe the observed pattern is due to S (M+2 ~ 4%) but the intensity 33% is high, maybe due to presence of two sulfurs? Two S would give M+2 ~8% still low. So likely chlorine.

Thus formula maybe C14H12ClO3? Compute: C14 168, H12 12.0939, Cl 34.9689, O3 47.9847 total = 263. (168+12.0939=180.0939; +34.9689=215.0628; +47.9847=263.0475). Not.

C15H14ClO3? 180+14.10955+34.9689+47.9847=277.06315. That's close to 276.0666 (difference -0.9965). If we consider [M+H]+ then neutral mass 275.059? Not.

Maybe the observed m/z is [M+H]+ of C15H13ClO3? Compute neutral mass: C15 180, H13 13.1017, Cl 34.9689, O3 47.9847 = 276.0553. Add proton 1.0073 = 277.0626. Not.

Our observed 276.0666 could be [M+H]+ of C15H13ClO2? Compute neutral: C15 180, H13 13.1017, Cl 34.9689, O2 31.9898 = 260.0604. +H = 261.0677. No.

Maybe the observed is [M+Na]+? Not.

Given we have proton NMR data: signals: 1.29 (t, 3H) and 4.30 (q, 2H) typical ethyl group (CH3-CH2-O). Aromatic region: 7.29 (dd, 4H), 7.75 (dd, 1H), 7.98 (ddd, 2H). Total aromatic protons = 7? 4+1+2 =7. So total protons observed: 3+2+7 =12. So molecule has 12 H observed. Possibly additional non-protonated hetero atoms.

Thus formula likely C? H12? plus maybe O and S/Cl.

Ethyl ester OCH2CH3 attached to aromatic ring. The aromatic pattern suggests a disubstituted benzene? 7 aromatic protons suggests maybe biphenyl? Actually biphenyl has 10 aromatic H. 7 suggests maybe phenyl attached to hetero group plus another phenyl? Let's think: Ethyl ester of benzoic acid gives aromatic 5 H. Here we have 7, suggests two aromatic rings with substitution pattern giving 7 total. Could be phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl? The SMILES we tried: CCOC(=O)C1=CC=C(S(=O)C2=CC=CC=C2)C=C1 (ethyl 4-(phenylsulfonyl)cinnamate?) That has aromatic protons: phenyl (5) + substituted phenyl (maybe 2). Total 7. Good. That matches NMR: ethyl group (CH3 triplet, CH2 quartet). Aromatic: 7 protons.

Thus our candidate SMILES matches NMR pattern. Mass: compute formula C15H14O3S? Wait our SMILES: CCOC(=O)C1=CC=C(S(=O)C2=CC=CC=C2)C=C1. Count: Ethyl ester: CCOC(=O)- gives C3H5O2? Actually ethyl ester of something: CCOC(=O) = C2H5O-CO- (C3H5O2). Then aromatic ring with two double bonds (cinnamate) adds C8H5? plus phenyl sulfone adds C6H5SO2? Let's compute total: C3 + C8 + C6 = C17? Wait need systematic.

Let's just get formula via tool: we got C15H14O3S from get_formula_from_smiles. That has 14 H, but NMR shows 12 H (observed). Maybe some H are exchangeable? Not.

But mass of C15H14O3S neutral = 274.0664, [M+H]+ = 275.0737, not 276.0666. Off by 1 Da. Could be sodium adduct [M+Na]+ = 297.0. Not.

Maybe the observed m/z is [M+H]+ of C15H15O3S (mass 275.0742 +1 = 276.0815) close to 276.0666 (difference 0.015). Could be measurement error. So formula C15H15O3S fits mass and isotopic pattern? But chlorine pattern suggests not. However chlorine pattern may be misinterpreted; M+2 intensity 33% could be due to presence of two 13C isotopes? 13C natural abundance 1.1% each, probability of two 13C ~ (nC choose 2)*(1.1%)^2 ~ for 15 C, about 105*0.0121% = 1.27% not 33%. So chlorine likely.

Our candidate lacks chlorine. So maybe the correct molecule contains chlorine, not sulfur. The isomers list includes many with Cl. Let's examine one: 'CC1=CC(=C(C=C1)C)COC2=CC=C(C=C2)S(=O)[O-]' includes sulfonate. Not chlorine.

But we need chlorine. Let's search among isomers list: I see none with Cl, they have S(=O)[O-] etc. So maybe the mass includes chlorine but we misinterpret isotopic pattern. Let's compute expected isotopic pattern for C15H15O3S: M+2 from 34S? Actually 34S abundance 4.21% gives M+2 ~4% of M. Observed 33.6% is much higher. So chlorine more likely.

Thus maybe formula C14H12ClO3? Let's compute mass: C14 168, H12 12.0939, Cl 34.9689, O3 47.9847 = 263.0475. Not 276.

Add another phenyl? C15H13ClO3? 180+13.1017+34.9689+47.9847=276.0553. That's close! So formula C15H13ClO3 (neutral). [M+H]+ = 277.0626. Observed 276.0666 maybe M+? So maybe observed is radical cation M+ of C15H13ClO3 (mass 276.0553). Observed 276.0666 diff 0.0113. Acceptable.

Thus candidate: ethyl 4-chlorocinnamate? Ethyl 4-chlorocinnamate would have formula C11H9ClO2? Not.

Our NMR shows ethyl group, aromatic 7 H, suggests two rings, one chlorine substituent maybe on phenyl. So structure: ethyl 4-chlorophenyl cinnamate? That would have two phenyl rings, one with Cl, one with ethyl ester. Count: Ethyl cinnamate (C11H12O2) plus phenyl chloride (C6H4Cl) attached via double bond? Actually cinnamate is phenyl attached to C=C-COOEt. So ethyl trans-cinnamate: C11H12O2. Add Cl on phenyl ring gives C11H11ClO2. That's C11? Wait need two phenyl rings? Cinnamate already has phenyl. So ethyl 4-chlorocinnamate formula C11H11ClO2? Let's compute: C11 (12*11=132), H11=11.086, Cl=34.969, O2=31.99 total = 210.045. Not.

Our formula C15H13ClO3 suggests three rings? Actually C15 suggests maybe phenyl-phenyl-COOEt? That's biphenyl with ethyl ester: C15H13O2? plus Cl? Let's think: Ethyl benzoate (C9H10O2). Add phenyl substituent (C6H5) gives C15H15O2. Add Cl replace H gives C15H14ClO2. Not O3.

Our candidate earlier CCOC(=O)C1=CC=C(S(=O)C2=CC=CC=C2)C=C1 has O3 and S. Not Cl.

Maybe the correct is ethyl 4-chlorophenyl sulfone? That would have S and Cl? Not.

Given limited time, maybe the best guess is the SMILES we already have, despite mass mismatch. The task is to extract SMILES efficiently; we have candidate. Could we validate via search? Use search_by_smiles for our candidate.
